#!/bin/bash

#FLUX --job-name=codellama_llamax_finetune
#FLUX --nodes=1
#FLUX --ntasks=1
#FLUX --cpus-per-task=10
#FLUX --mem-per-task=200G
#FLUX --gpus-per-task=4
#FLUX --queue=a100
#FLUX --qos=a100_wenhuchen
# NOTE: SLURM's -w (--nodelist) forces a job to run on a specific node. The Flux
# equivalent is to use a hostname constraint.
#FLUX -C hostname:gpu185
#FLUX --output={name}.{id}.log

## must export blow enviroment variables
export NCCL_IB_HCA=mlx5
export NCCL_IB_TC=136
export NCCL_IB_SL=5
export NCCL_IB_GID_INDEX=3
export NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=bond0
export NCCL_DEBUG=INFO
 

__conda_setup="$('/cpfs/29cd2992fe666f2a/user/huangwenhao/alex/miniconda3/bin/conda' 'shell.bash' 'hook' 2> /dev/null)"
if [ $? -eq 0 ]; then
    eval "$__conda_setup"
else
    if [ -f "/cpfs/29cd2992fe666f2a/user/huangwenhao/alex/miniconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh" ]; then
        . "/cpfs/29cd2992fe666f2a/user/huangwenhao/alex/miniconda3/etc/profile.d/conda.sh"
    else
        export PATH="/cpfs/29cd2992fe666f2a/user/huangwenhao/alex/miniconda3/bin:$PATH"
    fi
fi
unset __conda_setup

which conda
export HF_HOME=/cpfs/29cd2992fe666f2a/user/huangwenhao/alex/.cache/huggingface
cd /cpfs/29cd2992fe666f2a/user/huangwenhao/alex/uskg_eval/Llama-X/src
conda activate SKGLM

export WANDB_DISABLED=True

#MODEL_DIR=/ssd005/projects/waterloo_nlp/alex/Llama-2-7b-hf/
#MODEL_DIR=/ssd005/projects/waterloo_nlp/alex/llama2_8_18/before_restart/checkpoint-15380
MODEL_DIR=/cpfs/29cd2992fe666f2a/user/huangwenhao/alex/codellama/CodeLlama-7b-Instruct-hf
#MODEL_DIR=/h/wenhuchen/STORAGE/alex/codellama_finetune/checkpoint-25630
DATA_PATH=/cpfs/29cd2992fe666f2a/user/huangwenhao/alex/uskg_eval/llama_data_v11_kg_task_labels.json
OUTPUT_DIR=/cpfs/29cd2992fe666f2a/user/huangwenhao/alex/uskg_eval/models/llama/v11_kg_task_labels


# The original script relies on environment variables (MASTER_ADDR, WORLD_SIZE, etc.)
# that appear to be set by an external orchestrator. For a pure Flux environment
# on a single node, these are not needed. We simplify the launch to a standard
# single-node torchrun command, using the number of GPUs requested by the job.
LAUNCHER="torchrun"
LAUNCHER_ARGS=(--nproc_per_node=4)
SCRIPT="train_on_formatted.py"
SCRIPT_ARGS=(--model_name_or_path ${MODEL_DIR} \
    --data_path "${DATA_PATH}" \
    --output_dir ${OUTPUT_DIR} \
    --pkl_path "cl_2048_v11_task_labels.pkl" \
    --has_instruction True \
    --dataset_type="skg" \
    --num_train_epochs 3 \
    --model_max_length 2048 \
    --per_device_train_batch_size 16 \
    --per_device_eval_batch_size 1 \
    --gradient_accumulation_steps 2 \
    --evaluation_strategy no \
    --save_total_limit 3 \
    --save_strategy "epoch" \
    --learning_rate 2e-5 \
    --warmup_ratio 0.01 \
    --logging_steps 2 \
    --lr_scheduler_type cosine \
    --report_to "tensorboard" \
    --gradient_checkpointing True \
    --deepspeed configs/deepspeed_config_transformers4.31.json \
    --fp16 True
)

# The SLURM_PROCID variable is replaced by the Flux equivalent, FLUX_TASK_RANK.
echo 'Flux task rank:'${FLUX_TASK_RANK}
echo $LAUNCHER "${LAUNCHER_ARGS[@]}" $SCRIPT "${SCRIPT_ARGS[@]}"

$LAUNCHER "${LAUNCHER_ARGS[@]}" $SCRIPT "${SCRIPT_ARGS[@]}"

issues: The directive '#FLUX -C hostname:gpu185' hardcodes the job to a single, specific node ('gpu185'). This is generally an anti-pattern in shared computing environments as it prevents the scheduler from flexibly placing the job on any available node that meets the requirements. If 'gpu185' is busy, offline, or removed from the cluster, the job will fail to run or remain queued indefinitely. It is better to request generic features (e.g., `-C a100`) and let the scheduler find a suitable node.
